triggers: Spores released when raindrops or touch compress mature fruitbody; no fruiting rain/temperature thresholds stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat is forest only; sources also give grassy areas, roadsides, gardens, fields. Season June-Nov (de wiki) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation not stated (only subalpine Iceland/subarctic Greenland).

triggers: Fruits after hot, humid weather (en wiki); earliest-appearing bolete of the season (from May/June). No numeric thresholds.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources name only Fagus/Quercus as hosts (Carpinus appears only as forest type oak-hornbeam; Tilia not confirmed). Season extends to Oct vs catalogue May-Sep. Soil indifferent, fresh to moderately dry loam. Elevation not stated (Ro source: hill and mountain zones).

triggers: None stated. Associated with humus-rich soil and rotting wood, mulched gardens.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season early summer to late autumn per sources (catalogue Jun-Oct). Himalaya record to 3000 m only; no Carpathian elevation. Habitats broader: spruce, beech, oak-hornbeam, riparian forest, alder swamp, parks.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Nov (en wiki, single source) vs catalogue Jul-Nov. De wiki lists juniper heath, dry grassland, orchard meadows and light beech/oak-hornbeam woods (rarely hardwood floodplain): more open-grassland than catalogue edge-of-wood.

triggers: None stated; early-season (spring/early summer) species. Very rarely fruits in autumn.
conflicts_with_catalogue: De wiki gives May-July (rarely autumn) vs catalogue Apr-Jun. Substrate is wood chips, plant debris, grass, compost rather than grass alone. Elevation not stated.

triggers: Does not fruit in cold; warm-season species (summer to early autumn), appears later in summer than P. ostreatus. No numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources say summer and early autumn only (catalogue May-Oct is wider). Saprophyte and weak parasite; also on conifers in western N. America (en wiki). Hosts per de wiki: beech, ash, poplar, birch, walnut, Sorbus.

triggers: Prefers cooler weather; pioneer species on poor soils. No numeric thresholds.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No contradiction on season (Jun-Nov). Sources cite Pinaceae/Fagaceae/Betulaceae families generically; genera Pinus/Fagus/Betula inferred from family names and the en wiki text. Elevation not stated. Also heathland on nutrient-poor soil.

triggers: None stated; flesh becomes watery in rainy weather.
conflicts_with_catalogue: None on hosts or season (June-Oct per de wiki). Elevation not stated. En wiki notes occurrence in urban areas with ornamental birches.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources disagree on soil: de wiki says calcareous/alkaline only, en wiki says calcareous and acidic (left null). Season June-Oct (de) vs catalogue Jun-Nov. Elevation: coast to alpine zone, no numbers. De wiki: two-needle pines; light spots, parks, edges, sheep pastures.

triggers: Thermophilous; climate requirements similar to Boletus aereus. No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (de wiki) vs catalogue Jul-Sep. Abies not supported by sources (broadleaf partners: beech, oak, sweet chestnut). Calcareous preference ('haeufig auf kalkhaltigem Boden'), not 'calcareous or acid'. Elevation not stated. Rare, warmth-loving.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season June-Sept, early finds May (de wiki) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Picea/Pinus not named as hosts (sources: birch, beech, oak, poplar). Sandy soil confirmed; acidity not stated. Described as very rare in Germany, patchy; Romanian abundance unknown.

triggers: None stated; more abundant in younger or disturbed pine stands than mature ones.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Jul-Nov (de wiki) vs catalogue Aug-Nov. De wiki: predominantly lowland, rarely subalpine; en wiki: to 800 m in Alps; catalogue 300-1400 m not supported. Acidic preferred but also on calcareous soil.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources contradict each other on soil: de wiki says acid (pH<4), nutrient-poor, beech/fir-beech/spruce-fir forests; redlist.info says mature broadleaf woods with higher pH, beech/oak (also hazel, birch, hornbeam). Months not stated; catalogue unverified. Rare/red-listed.

triggers: Described as a dry-weather mushroom; fruits especially after dry summers and can be plentiful when other fungi are scarce. No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: De wiki: Aug-Dec vs catalogue Aug-Nov. Substrate also buried cones, moss, litter, burnt ground, wood chips. Mostly conifer, rarely pure broadleaf woods. Elevation not stated.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Fagus not supported as host (de wiki: spruce; en wiki: Pinus contorta, P. pinaster, Arctostaphylos). Season mostly June-Oct, from late May (de wiki) vs catalogue May-Oct. Sandy, acidic soil confirmed. Elevation not stated.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Soil conflict: de wiki calcareous; en wiki cites topsoil pH 5.0-6.6 in Swedish beech woods (left null). Season: from July (de) / late spring to autumn (en), end not given. Beech preferred but not an obligate host. Rare (de), threatened in Aland.

triggers: None stated; Scottish pine plantation study had August-October peak fruiting.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season July-Nov (de wiki) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation not stated, so catalogue 500-1700 m unverified. Acid, wet soils, often in Sphagnum, confirmed.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (de wiki) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Mountain spruce forests on acid soil confirmed; numeric elevation not stated (catalogue 800-1700 m unverified). Rare in Germany and red-listed; mushroom.world adds pine in N. America.

triggers: Abundance varies strongly between years; most abundant in warmer years with higher rainfall (en wiki). Sporadic.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No contradiction on hosts, calcareous soil or season (Aug-Oct). En wiki: preferentially montane, but no numeric elevation; catalogue 500-1500 m unverified. Rare overall.

triggers: None stated; fruits in autumn (en wiki).
conflicts_with_catalogue: De wiki gives early summer to late autumn, en wiki autumn; main season set Sep-Nov (catalogue Aug-Nov). Picea not named in the sources (named: Douglas-fir, true firs, pines, hemlock, mountain pine); also on hardwood in N. America. Elevation not stated.

triggers: Frost-resistant winter mushroom; fruits in cold months when most fungi stop. No temperature numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: De wiki: Sept-April; en wiki: Oct-Feb in Europe; overlap used (catalogue also includes March). Hosts per sources also include Fraxinus, Sambucus, Fagus, Quercus. Also on living trees and buried wood. Elevation not stated. Riparian habitat inferred from Salix/Populus preference, not stated.

triggers: Appears late in the year after the first night frosts ('herald of winter'); often in large groups. No temperature numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: None on host or season (Oct-Dec). Elevation not stated; catalogue 300-1500 m unverified.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No contradiction on season (Aug-Oct), acid wet Sphagnum soils or Picea/Pinus. Abies also host (de wiki); Fagus/bracken in France (en wiki). Elevation not given numerically (subalpine forests). Synonym C. speciosissimus. Not uncommon in S. Germany, uncommon in British Isles.

triggers: Spring species appearing after snowmelt (123pilzsuche); fruiting window March-May. No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat 'grassy woodland, conifer edges' (WG): sources describe mainly nutrient-poor grassland, hedges, gardens, pastures, heaths, only rarely woods. Conifer edges not supported. Season Mar-May confirmed. Elevation not stated.

triggers: Spring rainfall in March-May triggers fruiting (Romanian source); no amounts stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Romanian source: pastures and semi-arid zones, humus-rich sandy or clay soils, also neglected vineyards, shrubland, disturbed ground; may form mycorrhiza with conifer roots at forest margins. Regions Dobrogea/Moldova and elevation 0-400 m not confirmed. Season Mar-May confirmed (single source).

triggers: None stated. Fruitbodies unripe from June, ripe from September, persisting to Jan/Feb; Burgundy form Sep-Dec/Jan.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Romanian source: 200-1100 m (catalogue 100-900); hosts include Tilia, Carpinus, Quercus cerris/petraea, Acer campestre. Corylus not confirmed. Season Jun-Jan (Ro) vs catalogue May-Dec; en wiki gives summer form May-Aug.

triggers: Needs humid conditions (high air humidity forests); fruits near edges of old wounds in autumn. No numeric thresholds for fruiting.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Trophic: sources say saprotroph on dead wood/heartwood of old broadleaf trees (can colonize wounds of living trees); catalogue 'p' is weaker. Season Aug-Nov confirmed. Elevation not stated. Red-listed in many European countries.

triggers: None stated. Lives on wood chips, bark mulch, straw, rotting plant waste.
conflicts_with_catalogue: De wiki: spring and autumn with a marked summer fruiting gap (catalogue is continuous May-Oct); en wiki says summer-autumn in N. America. Months left null. Rare in Germany but spreading via mulch use. Elevation not stated.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts: beech primary but also spruce, fir, oak (catalogue Fagus only). Season late Jul-Nov (de wiki) vs catalogue Aug-Oct. Soil: de wiki tolerates calcareous and silicate; en wiki says acid, so set indifferent. Lowland to mountains, no numbers.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Accepted name given as Collybia phyllophila on de wiki (synonym Clitocybe phyllophila); not cross-checked against Index Fungorum. Season Sep-Nov (de), Jul-early Dec (UK). Litter especially spruce and beech; also grassy verges under hedges. Soil acid to basic, N-enriched.

triggers: None stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Carpinus not supported: de wiki says it grows only with hazel (Corylus), often in coppiced hazel stands. Season Aug-Oct (both sources) vs catalogue Aug-Oct unchanged; catalogue Jul start not an issue. Elevation not stated. Synonym L. hortensis.
